# x30_agent figures (generated by ros2_ws/src/x30_agent/scripts/make_figures.py from results/agent_live/*)

* `a1_live_eval.png` (live Qwen3-VL-8B Q4_K_M, llama.cpp, context 16384, one slot, RTX 3090 Ti). Left: share of the 9 hand-made states per type in which the model's first reply was the best next step
  (blue: raw reply; orange: after the harness fixes, i.e. a `verify` call without `question` gets the task as question, and in state F a synonym `search` is also accepted because the hint offers it).
  72 invented single-turn states (not the robot, not independent samples), tool_choice=auto; `required` gave identical numbers. Raw weak spots: C (all 9 replies chose `verify` correctly but omitted the
  required `question`) and F (7 of 9 searched a synonym instead of giving up). Right: mean latency per turn for a 3.4k-token prompt, 12 states: cold prompt cache 1.28 s, cached system prompt 0.28 s,
  and 0.32-0.39 s with 0, 1 or 2 small images in the cached case (images add only 60-100 prompt tokens at the fake world's small image size).
* `a2_fake_world_episodes.png` (FAKE pure-python world, live model; not the robot). Agent turns per episode, green = the agent claimed success and ended within 1.5 m of the target, red = otherwise.
  Top row object_nav (20 episodes each: text only, map+camera images, and with a verify skill that answers wrongly in 20 % of the calls). Bottom row velocity_follow (20 episodes each): target only
  ("Walk to the red table in the kitchen", camera only, no map; first prompt version), and a metric route description ("Turn left about 30 degrees, then walk forward about 5 meters ...") with the final prompt,
  once on the seeds used while tuning the follower prompt (dev) and once on fresh seeds. The fake world is easy for object_nav (all objects are revealed by the first 360 degree scan) and
  is not a model of real perception; do not read the green bars as robot performance.
